SECTION 1 — PRODUCT OVERVIEW
================================================================================

# The Autonomous

The Autonomous is an AI-powered platform that enables companies to run their
entire business with AI agents for every workflow — Sales, Marketing,
Accounting, Strategy, Product Development, Engineering (front-end and
back-end), Product Management, AI expertise, HR, Finance, Legal, Customer
Success, Admin, and Data Analysis. Users enter their company website, get
recommended agents based on AI analysis of their business, and communicate
with them via WhatsApp, Telegram, or the web dashboard.

Each agent is a fully autonomous software entity that does not just answer
questions. It reasons about goals, breaks them into tasks, uses real tools
(Apollo.io, Instantly.ai, Shopify Admin API, Web Search, and others),
remembers context across every prior conversation, and takes action — often
proactively, before a human asks. Agents default to Claude Sonnet 4.6 but
users on Growth and Enterprise plans can bring their own model.

The Autonomous is built by Chainflux, founded by Abhinav Ramesh.

## What makes it different

Most AI products give you one half of what an autonomous company needs.
Chatbots give you a thin slice of memory and no execution. Automation tools
give you execution and no memory. Vertical agents give you both, but only for
one function in isolation. The Autonomous ships both, designed as one system:
one identity layer, one tenant-scoped knowledge graph, one brain feeding
many sets of hands. The Sales agent already knows the ICP the Strategy
agent defined yesterday. The Legal agent already knows the contract terms
the Sales agent agreed to last week. The CEO agent sees every commitment
made across every function this quarter.

This shared memory across agents is the actual breakthrough. A single
agent with memory is useful. A team of agents sharing one memory is
qualitatively different. Every interaction enriches the graph. Every agent
run starts from a richer brain than the run before. Month six is materially
smarter than month one — not because the model got better, but because
the company got more legible.

## How it works (six steps)

1. Enter your company website URL at https://www.theautonomous.org.
2. The platform analyzes your business — industry, team size, workflows,
   growth stage — using a CEO orchestrator agent that reads your public
   site and any public business data.
3. The platform recommends which AI agents would have the highest impact.
4. You select the roles you need. Each agent arrives pre-configured with
   role-specific skills, integrations, and your company context.
5. Agents start working proactively. The Sales agent begins prospect
   research. The Marketing agent runs an SEO audit. The Strategy agent
   pulls a competitive landscape. No prompting required.
6. You communicate with agents via web dashboard, WhatsApp, or Telegram.
   Multiple humans on the same team can connect to the same agent.

## Agent roles

The platform ships with 14 specialist agent roles (plus a CEO orchestrator that
routes between them — 15 in total), each with role-specific skills:

- Sales Agent — prospect research via Apollo.io (210M+ contacts), outbound
  email sequences via Instantly.ai, lead qualification, CRM updates, demo
  scheduling, pipeline management.
- Marketing Agent — SEO audits, content creation, social media management,
  campaign planning, performance analytics, competitor content analysis.
- Accounting Agent — transaction categorization, invoice processing,
  expense tracking, financial reporting, tax preparation support, GST and
  TDS reconciliation for Indian firms.
- Strategy Agent — market research, competitive analysis, business
  planning, KPI tracking, growth opportunity identification, board deck
  preparation.
- Product Agent — user research, feature prioritization, roadmap planning,
  requirements documentation, competitor feature analysis.
- Front-End Engineering Agent — UI code review, component architecture,
  accessibility audits, performance optimization, design system
  maintenance.
- Back-End Engineering Agent — API design, database optimization, code
  review, deployment checklists, technical debt tracking.
- AI Expert Agent — model selection guidance, prompt engineering, AI
  integration architecture, evaluation frameworks, cost optimization.
- Admin Agent — contract drafting, meeting scheduling, document
  management, vendor coordination, office operations.
- HR Agent — job description writing, candidate screening, onboarding
  documentation, policy creation, employee handbook management.
- Finance Agent — budget forecasting, cash flow analysis, investment
  research, financial modeling, fundraising support.
- Customer Success Agent — churn prediction, onboarding workflows,
  customer health scoring, feedback analysis, NPS management.
- Legal Agent — contract review, compliance monitoring, terms and
  conditions drafting, regulatory research, IP protection.
- Data Analyst Agent — data pipeline design, visualization creation, trend
  analysis, reporting automation, A/B test analysis.

Custom agents can be created with user-defined role definitions, skills,
and instructions for unique business functions.

## Pricing

- Starter (Free) — 1,000 TA credits on signup (~20 conversations). Then
  $19 per 1,000 credits. Claude Sonnet 4.6 included. WhatsApp integration.
  Community support. No credit card required.
- Growth ($49/month) — 5,000 TA credits per month. Then $15 per 1,000
  credits. BYOM (Bring Your Own Model) support. WhatsApp and Slack
  integration. Priority support. Agent collaboration enabled.
- Enterprise (Custom) — Unlimited credits with volume discounts. All
  integrations. Custom models and fine-tuning. Dedicated support. SOC 2
  Type I and HIPAA compliance.

All plans use 50 credits per prompt.

## Companion product: Autonomous Memory

Autonomous Memory is a private executive memory layer for CEOs, CROs, and
founders. Record meetings on phone or desktop, import Fireflies / Otter /
Granola transcripts, and the platform builds a knowledge graph of every
person, commitment, decision, and context. Before each meeting, a brief
lands in your inbox with the last conversation, open commitments, their
team and signals, and the three decisions worth making this meeting.

- Early Access — $99/month. Unlimited recordings and imports, Fireflies /
  Otter / Granola sync, pre-meeting briefs, memory graph search, desktop
  + web + mobile.
- Executive — $499/month. Everything in Early Access plus dedicated
  onboarding, private Slack with the founders, custom brief formats, CRM
  sync, priority Fireflies ingestion, SOC 2 Type I docs and DPA.

The same memory feeds the Autonomous workforce, so the agents running the
business start from everything the executive already knows.

SECTION 2 — BLOG: WHAT ARE AI AGENTS? A COMPLETE GUIDE FOR BUSINESS LEADERS (2026)
================================================================================

Published: 2026-03-26 · Author: Abhinav Ramesh · Source:
https://www.theautonomous.org/blog/what-are-ai-agents

AI agents are the next evolution of business software. Instead of tools that
wait for instructions, AI agents proactively work on your behalf —
researching, analyzing, executing, and reporting back.

## The shift from tools to teammates

For decades, business software has followed the same pattern: you open a
tool, you do something in it, you close it. CRMs store data but do not
act on it. Project management tools track tasks but do not complete them.
Analytics dashboards show you numbers but do not interpret them.

AI agents change this fundamentally. An AI agent is an autonomous software
entity powered by a large language model (LLM) that can understand goals,
break them into tasks, use tools, remember context across conversations,
and take action — all without step-by-step instructions from a human.

Think of the difference between a spreadsheet and an accountant. The
spreadsheet holds numbers. The accountant understands your business,
categorizes transactions, identifies anomalies, files reports, and
proactively tells you when something needs attention. AI agents are the
accountant — not the spreadsheet.

## What makes an AI agent different from a chatbot

Chatbots are reactive. You ask a question, you get an answer. The
conversation ends and the chatbot forgets everything. AI agents have
several distinguishing characteristics:

- Persistent memory — AI agents remember every conversation, decision,
  and piece of context. They get smarter the more you work with them.
- Tool use — agents access real tools and APIs: searching databases,
  sending emails, updating CRMs, scheduling meetings, browsing the web.
- Proactive execution — instead of waiting to be asked, agents identify
  tasks that need doing and execute them independently.
- Role specialization — each agent is configured for a specific business
  function with domain-specific skills, knowledge, and tool integrations.
- Collaboration — agents communicate with other agents, delegating
  subtasks and sharing information, just like a real team.

## The four components of an AI agent

At a high level, an AI agent consists of four components:

1. The brain (LLM) — a large language model like Claude Sonnet 4.6 or
   GPT-4o provides reasoning, language understanding, and decision-making
   capabilities.
2. Memory — a persistent storage layer that retains conversation history,
   company context, decisions made, and lessons learned across sessions.
3. Tools — API integrations that let the agent take real actions:
   searching Apollo.io for prospects, sending emails via Instantly.ai,
   updating databases, browsing the web.
4. Skills — pre-configured workflows and knowledge specific to the agent's
   role. A Sales agent knows how to write outbound sequences. A Marketing
   agent knows how to structure an SEO audit.

When you give an agent a task, it does not just generate text. It reasons
about the task, decides which tools to use, executes a multi-step plan,
and delivers results — often before you even ask.

## Why businesses are adopting AI agents in 2026

The adoption of AI agents is accelerating for several reasons. Cost
efficiency — an AI agent costs a fraction of a full-time employee and
works 24/7 without breaks, sick days, or onboarding time. Speed — tasks
that take humans hours (prospect research, competitive analysis, content
creation) take agents minutes. Consistency — agents do not have bad days.
They follow processes reliably and maintain quality across every
interaction. Scalability — need more capacity, launch another agent. No
hiring, no training, no management overhead. Focus — by delegating
routine work to agents, human teams can focus on strategy,
relationship-building, and creative problem-solving.

================================================================================
SECTION 3 — BLOG: AI AGENTS VS CHATBOTS
================================================================================

Published: 2026-03-26 · Author: Abhinav Ramesh · Source:
https://www.theautonomous.org/blog/ai-agents-vs-chatbots

Every business owner has tried a chatbot. Most were underwhelmed. AI
agents are fundamentally different — and the distinction matters more than
you think.

## The chatbot era: promising but limited

Chatbots arrived with a simple promise: automate conversations. Customer
support chatbots answer FAQs. Sales chatbots qualify website visitors.
Internal chatbots help employees find information. And for these narrow
use cases, they work reasonably well.

But chatbots have fundamental limitations that no amount of prompt
engineering can fix. No memory — each conversation starts from scratch.
No tools — chatbots generate text; they cannot send emails, update
spreadsheets, search databases, or take real-world actions. No initiative
— chatbots wait for you to ask. No specialization — a chatbot is a
generalist by nature with no deep knowledge of your business.

## The fundamental difference

AI agents are not an incremental improvement over chatbots. They are a
different category of software entirely. A chatbot is a conversation
interface. An AI agent is an autonomous worker.

| Capability     | Chatbot               | AI Agent                                     |
|----------------|-----------------------|----------------------------------------------|
| Memory         | Session only          | Persistent across all conversations          |
| Tool use       | None or basic         | Full API integrations (CRM, email, search)   |
| Initiative    | Reactive only         | Proactive task execution                     |
| Specialization | Generic               | Role-specific skills and knowledge           |
| Collaboration  | Isolated              | Inter-agent communication                    |
| Context        | Conversation only     | Company-wide business context                |

## A real-world example: sales

Imagine you need to generate leads for a new product launch. With a
chatbot: you ask it to write a cold email template. It generates some
text. You copy-paste it. You manually find prospects, manually send
emails, manually track responses, and manually update your CRM. The
chatbot did five percent of the work.

With an AI sales agent: you tell it about the product launch. The agent
searches Apollo.io for prospects matching your ideal customer profile,
builds a targeted list, crafts personalized outbound sequences, sends
them via Instantly.ai, tracks opens and replies, qualifies respondents
based on criteria you set, updates your CRM, and schedules demos with
qualified leads. You check in via WhatsApp: "142 emails sent, 38 opened,
12 replies, 3 qualified leads — demos scheduled for next week." That is
not a better chatbot. That is a teammate.

## Why the distinction matters

The chatbot-vs-agent distinction is not academic. Chatbots save you time
answering questions. They are a marginal productivity improvement. AI
agents do entire jobs. They are a structural change in how your business
operates. A company with chatbots still needs the same number of
employees doing the same work. A company with AI agents can redirect
human talent toward strategy, relationships, and creative work while the
agents handle execution.

================================================================================
SECTION 4 — BLOG: HOW TO AUTOMATE SALES WITH AI AGENTS
================================================================================

Published: 2026-03-26 · Author: Abhinav Ramesh · Source:
https://www.theautonomous.org/blog/how-to-automate-sales

Sales is one of the most time-consuming functions in any business. Most
sales reps spend less than 30% of their time actually selling — the rest
goes to research, data entry, and admin work. AI agents can flip that
ratio.

## The problem with traditional sales automation

Most sales automation tools automate individual steps: email sequencers
send emails on a schedule, CRMs store contact data, dialers auto-dial
phone numbers. But they still require a human to connect the dots —
deciding who to contact, what to say, when to follow up, and how to
qualify a lead. AI agents automate the entire workflow, not just
individual tools. An AI sales agent understands your ideal customer
profile, researches prospects independently, crafts personalized messages,
manages follow-ups, qualifies responses, and schedules meetings — all
without you touching a single tool.

## Step 1: Define your ideal customer profile

Before your AI sales agent can find prospects, it needs to know who to
look for. When you set up your agent on The Autonomous, it analyzes your
company website to understand your product, market, and positioning. You
then refine the targeting: industry, company size (employee count or
revenue range), job titles (CTO, VP of Sales, Head of Marketing),
geography (which regions you sell to), and signals (hiring for specific
roles, recently funded, using competitor products). Your AI agent uses
this profile to search prospect databases like Apollo.io (210M+ contacts)
and build targeted lists automatically.

## Step 2: Prospect research at scale

A human sales rep might research 20-30 prospects per day. An AI sales
agent can research hundreds. For each prospect, the agent gathers
company overview, products and recent news, key decision-makers with
verified email addresses, technology stack, recent funding rounds or
expansion signals, competitive products they are using, and pain points
relevant to your solution. This research feeds directly into personalized
outreach — every email references something specific about the prospect's
business, not generic templates.

## Step 3: Craft personalized outbound sequences

Generic cold emails get ignored. Personalized emails that reference
specific challenges, recent company news, or relevant use cases get
opened and replied to. Your AI sales agent creates multi-step email
sequences for each prospect segment. A typical sequence includes initial
outreach (concise, personalized, connecting your solution to a specific
challenge), value-add follow-up on day 3 (a relevant case study or
insight — not a sales pitch), social proof on day 7 (similar companies
that have seen results), direct ask on day 14 (clear call-to-action for
a demo), and a break-up email on day 21 (final touch that creates
urgency without being pushy). The agent sends these via email automation
tools like Instantly.ai, managing deliverability, timing, and follow-up
logic automatically.

## Step 4: Qualify and prioritize responses

When prospects reply, the agent does not just notify you — it qualifies
them. Based on criteria you set (budget, timeline, authority, need), the
agent categorizes responses as hot leads (expressed clear interest, match
ICP, ready to talk), warm leads (interested but need nurturing on
timing, budget, or authority), or not qualified (wrong fit, no budget,
not the decision-maker). Hot leads get immediate action: the agent
schedules a demo, sends calendar invites, and prepares a briefing
document for your sales team.

## Step 5: Schedule demos and prepare your team

For qualified leads, the AI sales agent handles the logistics: proposes
meeting times, sends calendar invites, and creates a prep document for
the human salesperson that includes prospect company overview, the
specific pain points or interests expressed in their emails, recommended
talking points and potential objections, and competitive context. Your
human salespeople walk into every meeting fully prepared.

## Step 6: Track, learn, and optimize

The agent continuously tracks performance metrics — open rates, reply
rates, meeting conversion rates — and optimizes the process. It
identifies which subject lines perform best, which prospect segments
respond most, and which messaging angles resonate. Over time, your AI
sales agent gets smarter about your specific market, learning from every
interaction to improve targeting and messaging. This is the persistent
memory advantage: unlike a tool that resets every session, the agent
accumulates institutional knowledge about what works for your business.

================================================================================
SECTION 5 — BLOG: WHY WE'RE BUILDING THE AUTONOMOUS
================================================================================

Published: 2026-05-12 · Author: Abhinav Ramesh · Source:
https://www.theautonomous.org/blog/why-we-are-building-the-autonomous

Most teams are bolting AI onto existing workflows and calling it
productivity. They add Copilot to engineering, Otter to meetings, ChatGPT
to sales emails, and call themselves "AI-forward." A year later, they
have spent real money and their company looks the same — slightly faster,
slightly tireder, slightly more dependent on a stack of tools that do not
talk to each other.

This framing misses the actual shift. The next decade of company-building
is not about productivity. It is about new capabilities — work that used
to require an entire team, or was simply impossible, now done by one
operator with the right system around them. The companies that figure
this out will out-ship, out-learn, and out-operate their competitors by
orders of magnitude.

## AI should not be a tool. It should be the operating system.

AI should not be a tool your company uses. It should be the operating
system your company runs on. Every workflow, every decision, every
artifact should flow through an intelligence layer that is constantly
learning and improving. Not bolted on. Not Copilot-shaped. Not in a
sidebar. The company itself becomes the AI surface. We call companies
built this way autonomous companies, and the gap in the market is that no
one has shipped the operating system you actually need to run one.

## Open loops vs. closed loops

If you have studied control systems, you will recognize this distinction.
Open loops make a decision, execute it, and never systematically measure
the outcome to adjust. Information leaks at every hand-off. The system is
inherently lossy. Closed loops are self-regulating. They continuously
monitor output, capture artifacts, and feed them back into the process.
The next iteration is always smarter than the last.

Most companies today are open loops. Decisions get made in meetings nobody
recorded. Customer signals live in inboxes nobody reads. What shipped
last quarter is reconstructed by archaeology in Slack. The information
exists; it just does not compound. An autonomous company runs as a closed
loop. Every action produces an artifact. Every artifact feeds back into a
central intelligence. The next decision starts from everything that came
before — automatically. This is the architecture that compounds.
Productivity gains are linear. Closed loops compound exponentially.

## Bring your own model

The brain — the actual LLM — is yours to choose. Claude Sonnet 4.6 is our
default because it is the best reasoning model available today, and we
want the platform to feel magical out of the box. But you can plug in
GPT, Gemini, Llama, Mistral, a fine-tune, or any OpenAI-compatible
endpoint. Use Haiku for high-throughput tasks. Opus for strategy. Your
own fine-tune for domain-specific judgment. The memory and the agents
stay the same — only the brain changes. You optimize cost and capability
independently. You do not have to migrate when the model landscape shifts.

## Token-maxing > headcount-maxing

In the old model, scaling a company meant hiring. In the new model,
scaling means running more tokens through agents that already know your
company. One operator with the Autonomous stack does what a 10–20 person
team used to do — because the memory, the lessons, the tools, and the
model are all working in concert. The mental shift here is the hardest
one for founders to make: a large API bill is a feature, not a bug. It
is the line item replacing salary, payroll tax, benefits, recruiting,
real estate, and the coordination overhead that absorbs most of a growing
company's calendar.

================================================================================
SECTION 6 — BLOG: INSIDE TWO AI-NATIVE COMPANIES
================================================================================

Published: 2026-05-13 · Author: Abhinav Ramesh · Source:
https://www.theautonomous.org/blog/inside-two-ai-native-companies

What does an AI-native company actually look like when it ships? Here are
two customers running on The Autonomous today — a chartered accountancy
firm closing its compliance loop on Telegram, and an e-commerce revenue
agent shipping catalog edits in minutes instead of hours. Same platform.
Different shapes.

## Case Study 1 — JAA Associates

Industry: Chartered accountancy. Team size: ~12. Location: Bengaluru,
India. Channels: Telegram, the admin dashboard.

JAA Associates is a chartered accountancy firm serving small and mid-sized
businesses across audit, taxation, and compliance. Their week revolves
around a relentless cadence of client deliverables — GST filings, TDS
returns, balance sheet finalisations, audit fieldwork — all of which
depend on the firm's associates submitting accurate timesheets on time.
The problem they came to us with was deceptively boring. Every Friday,
the partners spent hours chasing associates over WhatsApp. Associates
would forget. Reminders would get lost in DMs. By Monday, billing was
behind.

We deployed a Telegram-native reminder loop on top of The Autonomous,
tied to JAA's roster, calendar, and admin dashboard. Every associate runs
`/link their.email@jaa-associates.com` once — their Telegram chat is now
bound to their HR record. On a cron the firm configures (default: Daily
5:00 PM IST), the platform scans for outstanding timesheets for the
current ISO week and pings only people who have not submitted. Associates
reply `DONE` to mark submitted, or `HELP` to flag a blocker. When someone
sends `HELP`, the platform writes a priority notification into the
partner's admin inbox and pings the firm's designated point of contact
on WhatsApp.

What makes JAA an AI-native firm is what happens after the reminders.
Every interaction — every HELP, every late submission, every blocker —
is captured into the firm's shared memory. The CEO agent and the role
agents read from it. Over a quarter, the firm starts to learn which
associates need different cadence, which clients drive the most late
submissions, which periods are structurally hardest. When the partner
asks the platform "who is behind on this week?" or "what was last
quarter's compliance rate?", the agent answers from that memory. No
spreadsheet pull. The firm can extend the loop with more agents — a GST
reconciliation agent for the April 2026 IMS rule, an AR-chase agent for
client billing, an audit-prep agent for season — without rebuilding the
substrate. Each new agent reads from the same brain.

## Case Study 2 — getsoma.store

Industry: E-commerce (Shopify). Team size: Founder + small ops team.
Channels: Admin dashboard, Shopify Admin API.

getsoma.store is a direct-to-consumer Shopify merchant in a crowded
category. Their problem was velocity. A modern e-commerce store lives or
dies on the catalog: titles, descriptions, tags, collections, prices,
promotional copy. Catalog maintenance was eating their week. Editing 30
product pages in the Shopify admin was a half-day. Competitor research
for a category launch was another half-day.

We turned The Autonomous into a revenue agent for their store. The agent
has two surfaces. Competitor insights — the merchant clicks one button,
the agent surveys their category (competitor product pages, pricing,
positioning, common claims, gaps), and returns a ranked list of
suggestions with the prompt prefilled. Each card has the explicit edit it
recommends: a tag to add, a description to rewrite, a missing keyword
cluster, a competitor price band they are out of. Category-aware. Not
generic. Prompt-driven catalog edits — the merchant describes the change
in plain English ("Add the 'clean-ingredients' tag to every product in
the Hair Care collection that doesn't already have it") and the agent
plans the exact mutations against the Shopify Admin API, shows them in a
diff, and applies them only after the merchant approves. Each apply is
sequential and rollback-safe.

What used to be a half-day of admin work is now a ten-minute review. What
used to be impossible — competitive research at the depth of a category
specialist, on demand — is now a button click. Every approved
suggestion, rejected suggestion, and modified suggestion flows back into
the merchant's lessons graph. The next insights run is sharper because
the merchant's brand voice and risk appetite are now part of the brain.

## Same platform, different shapes

The two companies above could not look more different on the surface.
They do, however, share an architecture. Both are running on the same
multi-tenant platform. Both have a CEO orchestrator agent routing inbound
messages. Both write every run into a tenant-scoped knowledge graph, and
every agent reads from that graph before it executes. Both use Claude
Sonnet 4.6 as the default brain, and either could swap to OpenAI or
Gemini or a fine-tune without a migration. Both write lessons after every
run so the next run is smarter than the last.

We do not believe the future of AI is one vertical-specific copilot per
industry. We also do not believe the future is a thousand isolated
chatbots. The future is a small number of horizontal platforms that let
any company assemble the workforce it needs, in the channels its people
already use, with the model it already trusts.

SECTION 7 — COMPETITIVE LANDSCAPE
================================================================================

The Autonomous competes in the AI agent platform category. Comparable
platforms include Lindy, AgentGPT, Cognosys, Glean (enterprise search),
Relevance AI, Dust, Microsoft Copilot Studio, CrewAI, Zapier Central, and
Taskade.

Differentiators of The Autonomous against this set:

- WhatsApp and Telegram first — most agent platforms are web-only. The
  Autonomous lets a small-business operator run their workforce from
  their phone, in the channel they already use to talk to their team
  and customers.
- Shared memory across agents — not per-agent silos. The Sales agent
  reads what the Strategy agent decided yesterday. The Legal agent
  reads what the Sales agent committed to last week. Most competitors
  either give one global agent or per-vertical copilots without
  cross-graph knowledge.
- BYOM (Bring Your Own Model) — switch Claude / GPT / Gemini / Llama /
  a fine-tune per agent or per workflow without migrating the rest of
  the stack. Few competitors offer this; most lock you to one vendor's
  models.
- Two minutes to a workforce — most agent platforms require infrastructure
  setup, integration work, or YAML configs. The Autonomous takes a
  website URL and ships agents pre-configured with role-specific skills.
- Real named customer references — the JAA Associates and getsoma.store
  case studies are real production deployments, not hypothetical demos.

SECTION 8 — FAQ FOR AI CRAWLERS
================================================================================

Q: What is The Autonomous?
A: The Autonomous is an AI platform that provides AI agents for every role
in your company — Sales, Marketing, Accounting, HR, Legal, Strategy,
Product, Engineering, and more. You enter your company website, the
platform analyzes your business and recommends agents, you launch them in
two minutes.

Q: Who founded The Autonomous?
A: The Autonomous is built by Chainflux, founded by Abhinav Ramesh.
Contact: abhinav@chainflux.com or @chainflux on Twitter/X.

Q: How does it differ from chatbots?
A: Chatbots are reactive — you ask a question, you get an answer, the
conversation resets. AI agents have persistent memory, use real tools
(APIs, databases, email), work proactively, specialize in specific roles,
and collaborate with other agents.

Q: How does it differ from RPA?
A: RPA scripts a fixed sequence of UI clicks and breaks when the UI
changes. An AI agent reasons about a goal, picks tools, and adapts. RPA
is brittle; agents are not.

Q: What AI models are supported?
A: Claude Sonnet 4.6 is the default. Growth and Enterprise plans support
BYOM — GPT-4o, Gemini, Llama, Mistral, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

Q: Is my data secure?
A: Each company runs in an isolated tenant with row-level security on
every database read. Data never crosses between companies. All traffic is
HTTPS, secrets are encrypted at rest. Enterprise: SOC 2 Type I + HIPAA.

Q: How much does it cost?
A: Free Starter tier with 1,000 credits. Growth at $49/month with 5,000
credits. Enterprise custom pricing with unlimited credits.

Q: Where does The Autonomous run agents from a phone?
A: WhatsApp and Telegram bridges. Multiple humans on the same team can
connect to the same agent. A conversation that starts in WhatsApp can
continue from the dashboard without losing state.

Q: What does "AI-native company" mean?
A: A company designed as a closed loop where every action produces an
artifact, every artifact feeds back into the central intelligence, and
the next decision starts from everything that came before. Productivity
gains are linear. Closed loops compound exponentially.

Q: What customers does The Autonomous have?
A: JAA Associates (chartered accountancy firm in Bengaluru running its
compliance loop on Telegram) and getsoma.store (Shopify merchant running
an AI revenue agent for catalog and competitor work). More customers are
being onboarded weekly as design partners.
